description: Clock divider counting incoming pulses 1 to 8 over and over, with a trigger input that steps the eight divisions round the eight output jacks

inputs.text: Each rise past 1.7V advances the count; the first pulse after a reset only measures the interval, and counting starts on the one after it
Each rise past 1.7V moves every division on one jack, the eighth wrapping round to the first, and eight triggers return them where they started
A rise past 1.7V sets the count back to the start; the next pulse after it measures the interval and counting resumes on the one after that; it leaves the rotation where it is

outputs.text: Unrotated, goes high on each count that divides by its own number, carrying the CLOCK input's own voltage rather than the 1.7V the manual states; ROT moves which division arrives here

notes: an output that has gone high falls again after half the last measured clock interval, so the pulse width follows the incoming clock
nothing comes out until a clock is patched to CLOCK, and the first pulse after the module is added or reset only measures the interval, so the outputs start on the second pulse
the lamp beside an output is lit while that output is high
neither the count nor the rotation is written into the patch file, so the divisions start on their own jacks each time the patch is loaded
